subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should Mission Control expose workspace-wide editing and/or host system filesystem browsing, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which files operator clients can read and write, crosses a deliberate allowlist boundary, and partly overlaps an open broader workspace-management design.

options.title: Approve Workspace API First
options.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped API/UI with explicit read/admin scopes, fs-safe confinement, size limits, destructive-operation UX, and proof while deferring system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap Files Only
options.body: Preserve the current `agents.files.*` allowlist and rely on read-only workspace/session previews until maintainers approve a broader file-management contract.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Open a separate security-reviewed host filesystem design with explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX before any system browser is implemented.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace API First
recommendation.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped API/UI with explicit read/admin scopes, fs-safe confinement, size limits, destructive-operation UX, and proof while deferring system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace API and chat file viewer that partially address the issue, making them the clearest owner for the remaining scope/security choice.
